newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ govt surplus NZ$597 mln in 4 months to Oct.
newsitem.headline: NZ govt surplus NZ$597 mln in 4 months to Oct.

text.p: The New Zealand government said on Friday it posted a NZ$597 million operating budget surplus for the four months to October 30, 1996, against a forecast surplus of $780 million.
Net public debt as a percentage of GDP was 30.9 percent at October 30 against 32.4 percent at June 30.
Tax revenue was 2.7 percent lower than forecast.
Treasury said tax revenue was $290 million lower than forecast due mainly to company tax and source deductions revenue being lower than forecast.
Total revenue was NZ$11.43 billion, two percent lower than forecast.
Net public debt at $27.35 billion was $127 million or 0.5 percent greater than forecast, and $1.3 billion (4.5 percent) lower than net public debt at June 30, 1996.
Treasury said the significant reduction in net public debt since June 30, 1996 was principally due to the proceeds from the sale of Forestry Corporation.

Treasury said net public debt was greater than forecast mainly due to lower-than-forecast taxation receipts ($163 million), partly offset by lower-than-forecast net purchases of physical assets ($25 million).
Expenses were were $10.89 billion. Expenses (excluding net foreign exchange gains) were 0.6 percent or $61 million higher than forecast.

*The net surplus, less distributions, attributable to State- owned enterprises and Crown entities, which was $98 million greater than forecast, mainly due to higher-than-forecast Crown entity net surpluses.
*Non-tax revenue was $61 million greater than forecast.
The government's net worth as at October 31 was $4.1 billion, $24 million lower than forecast and $756 million higher than at June 30, 1996.
The improvement in the Crown balance since June 30 was due to the operating balance of $597 million and net asset revaluations of $159 million, Treasury said.
Net cash flows from operating and investing activities were $126 million, compared with a forecast inflow of $170 million. Treasury said this was largely due to:

*lower-than-forecast net cash inflows from operations of $172 million, largely due to lower-than-forecast tax receipts, which were largely offset by higher-than-forecast net sales on investments ($133 million).
The financial statements for the five months ended November 30 1996, together with the monthly forecast track for the remainder of the financial year, would be released on January 17, 1997.
